To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the EQ-5d is a reliable and valid instrument to measure HRQoL among patients with T2DM in Canada, and 2) the disutility values associated with diabetes-related complications can be used to estimate the impact on HRQoL of these events in economic evaluations.
the greatest reductions in HRQL are associated with kidney failure (−10.2%) and myocardial infarctions (−5.9%).

the presence of diabetes-related complications is associated with reductions in health utility values, with the greatest impact associated with kidney failure, and that the utility values estimated here can be used in cost-effectiveness analyses to assess the outcome and value of interventions that reduce the incidence or severity of diabetes-related complications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
estimating the disutility associated to experiencing a diabetes-related complications for patients with diabetes.
the impact of diabetes complications on the health-related quality of lives of individuals with diabetes.
the estimation of the impact of diabetic complications on HRQL in patients with type 1 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the utility values calculated here are useful for assessing the outcome of interventions to reduce the incidence of complications in diabetes and for future economic evaluations of interventions to prevent diabetes complications in Canada.
diabetes is a disease which can have a significant impact on the quality of life of those suffering from it.

the results of this study suggest that the EQ-5-D is a useful tool for assessing health-related quality of live in patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and the disutility associated diabetes-related complications is significant and should be included in economic analyses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study provides the first estimate of the disutility associated to diabetes-related complications for patients with type-2 diabetes in Ontario.
we estimated the disutility associated to several diabetes-related complications and that the greatest impact on health-related quality oflife was kidney failure and myocardial infarctions.

the disutility associated to diabetes-related complications is significant and that this should be taken into account in the design of future economic evaluations of new treatments for type 2 diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disutility associated to diabetes-related complications is substantial and should be considered in future economic evaluations of interventions for type 2 diabetes management.
the disutility associated to a complication is dependent on both its severity and the patient's baseline health.
diabetes-related complications are associated with significant reductions in HRQL and that the greatest reductions in HRQL are associated with kidney failure, MI, and stroke.
